moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain the process of organizing and managing tests effectively using the Test Library and Shared Steps Library to improve reusability and efficiency.
Describe how to track changes with Revisions to maintain control over test versions and ensure accuracy.
Articulate how to create and manage Test Plans for web applications to streamline and structure your testing process.
Use Test Suites to group and execute tests efficiently, and use Auto Improve/Smart Locators and Bug Reporting to improve test reliability and collaboration.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Test Library: folders, labels, and test status

elements.description: Folders (create via + → New Folder) give tests a single-location home in the Test Library. Labels are applied/removed via Edit Labels (or right-click → Edit Labels) and, unlike folders, a test can carry several at once — better suited to cross-cutting groupings like 'smoke' or 'checkout'. Search the library with label:<name> to filter by a label.

Testim's built-in test statuses are Draft (not ready to be used yet — still in progress), Active (automatically applied to tests that ran in the last 30 days), Evaluating (ready, but stability still needs to be examined), and Quarantine (unstable — generating errors, waiting to be fixed). 'Failed' and 'Archived' are NOT Testim test statuses — 'Failed' describes a run's result, not the test's lifecycle status, and there is no 'Archived' status.

bulletPoints: Folders = single-location; Labels = multi-tag, searchable via label:<name>.
Real test statuses: Draft, Active, Evaluating, Quarantine — NOT 'Failed' or 'Archived'.
Active is auto-applied based on having run in the last 30 days; Quarantine flags unstable, error-generating tests.

elements.description: Clicking Advanced filters opens the Filter Shared Steps pane, letting you filter by step category (Groups, Actions, Validations, Wait for) — the same filtering pattern used elsewhere in Testim's library views, including surfacing steps that are otherwise hidden from the default view so they can be selected and unhidden.

Every time a test with changes is saved, the version before the change is automatically stored as a revision — no action is required to create one; it happens by itself on every save. After saving, a dialog optionally prompts for a change message describing the purpose of the change. The revision list (change message, user, date) lets you always look back and revert to an older revision.

bulletPoints: Shared Steps Library: Advanced filters → filter by Groups / Actions / Validations / Wait for (including finding hidden steps to unhide).
Revisions are created automatically on every save — not manually, not on close, and not by reusing a locally saved file.

elements.description: Test Plans model genuine environment setup/teardown around a run — preparing the environment before tests start, and cleaning up after. A Test Plan can be integrated with a CI tool by picking the specific CI tool your team uses and executing the test plan through that tool's pipeline, rather than being limited to local-only execution or manual copying of test cases.

Test Suites group tests into a collection and let you control the order they run in — the two core benefits: organizing tests into collections, and running multiple tests in sequence in a defined order. (Order is only guaranteed for non-parallel runs — passing --parallel to a suite run no longer guarantees the sequence.) Test Suites do not automatically delete unused tests, and executing directly from CI tools is a separate CLI/CI-integration concern, not a Test Suite feature itself.

bulletPoints: Test Plans: setup/teardown around a run; integrate with CI by picking a specific CI tool and running the plan through it.
Test Suites: group tests into collections + control run order — not auto-deletion, not itself a CI-execution mechanism.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Locators: Auto Improve and Smart Locator confidence

elements.description: If a locator's score drops below 70%, Testim automatically attempts to improve that locator to enhance the test's stability. If the improvement succeeds, Testim replaces the degraded locator with the improved one and creates a test revision labeled 'Testim auto improve' — so the change is tracked, not silent.

elements.term: Smart Locator confidence and changed attributes
elements.description: Smart Locators weight potentially hundreds of attributes per element. When an element's attributes change during a test run, the test can still pass — Smart Locators can typically still identify the element using its other, unchanged attributes — but the confidence score for that locator may decrease. A page-change warning is shown specifically when that confidence level varies by more than 20% compared to the originally recorded test.

bulletPoints: Locator score < 70% → Testim auto-attempts an improvement, tracked as a 'Testim auto improve' revision if it succeeds.
Changed element attributes during a run: the test may still pass, but the confidence score can decrease — not an automatic fail or skip.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Bug Reporting with the Testim Extension

elements.description: The Testim (Chrome) Extension's Capture feature records a video of a bug scenario, generates a screenshot per step, and can publish it straight to a connected bug tracker (e.g. Jira, Trello). Before any of that is possible, the prerequisite is installing the Testim browser extension for Chrome — the capture/video functionality lives inside the extension, not the web editor itself.

bulletPoints: Bug capture (video + screenshots) is a Testim Chrome Extension feature.
Installing the extension is the first, required step — before enabling any capture settings or connecting a bug tracker template.

examPitfalls.title: Treating 'Failed' or 'Archived' as Testim test statuses
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a test's lifecycle status can be set to 'Failed' or 'Archived' in the Test Library.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The real statuses are Draft, Active, Evaluating, and Quarantine. 'Failed' describes a run's outcome, not a test's status, and there is no 'Archived' status.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to manually trigger a revision
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for a button to explicitly 'create a revision' before making a change.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Revisions are created automatically every time a changed test is saved — there's no manual toggle or trigger needed.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming Test Suite order is always guaranteed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Relying on a Test Suite's configured order while also running it with --parallel.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Order is only guaranteed for non-parallel Test Suite runs — passing --parallel means the run order is no longer guaranteed.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to capture a bug video without the Testim extension installed
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for video-capture bug reporting inside the web-based editor alone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Capture Video & Bug Scenario is a Testim Chrome Extension feature — install the extension first; it's the prerequisite, not an optional add-on.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following is NOT an option for test status in the Testim test library?

options.text: Draft
Evaluating
Active
Failed
Archived

practiceQuiz.hint: The real statuses are Draft, Active, Evaluating, and Quarantine.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim's test statuses are Draft, Active, Evaluating, and Quarantine. 'Failed' is a run outcome, not a test status, and 'Archived' isn't a Testim status at all — both D and E are NOT valid options.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must you do to unhide a Shared Step in Testim?

options.text: Use the advanced filter to show hidden steps, then select the step and unhide it
Edit the step's properties and remove the hidden flag
Search for the step and select "Unhide" from the dropdown menu
Re-add the step to the test case from the hidden list

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same Advanced filters entry point used elsewhere in the Shared Steps Library.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Advanced filters pane is Testim's standard mechanism for surfacing items that aren't shown by default — including hidden shared steps — so you can select one and unhide it, rather than editing raw properties, a dropdown 'Unhide' command, or re-adding from a separate hidden list.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can you integrate a test plan with a CI tool in Testim?

options.text: Test plans cannot be integrated with CI tools.
Select the test plan and run it on the local machine.
Pick a specific CI tool and execute the test plan on that tool.
Manually copy test cases to the CI tool environment.

practiceQuiz.hint: Testim integrates natively with major CI/CD platforms — you pick the one your team uses.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A test plan is integrated with CI by picking the specific CI tool (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, etc.) your team uses and executing it through that tool's pipeline — not a local-only run, manual copying, or 'not possible'.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can a user create a revision?

options.text: Revisions are created automatically whenever changes are made to the test
The user can toggle the revisions button while saving a test to create
A revision will be created every time the user closes Testim
User's can use a previously saved test from their local drive

practiceQuiz.hint: No manual action is needed — it happens on save.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Every time a changed test is saved, the prior version is automatically stored as a revision — there's no manual toggle, no revision tied to closing the app, and no local-drive file involved.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What are the benefits of using Test Suites in Testim?

options.text: Organizing tests into collections.
Running multiple tests in sequence.
Deleting unused tests automatically.
Executing tests directly from CI tools.

practiceQuiz.hint: The two core benefits are about grouping and ordering, not deletion or CI execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Test Suites group tests into collections and let you control the order multiple tests run in. They don't auto-delete unused tests, and direct CI execution is a separate CLI/CI-integration concern, not a Test Suite benefit itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens when the locator score falls below a particular threshold in Testim?

options.text: The test will fail immediately.
Testim automatically attempts to improve the locator to enhance test stability.
The test will skip the element with the low locator score.
The locator will be deleted from the test.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is the Locators: Auto Improve mechanism, triggered below a specific score.
practiceQuiz.rationale: When a locator's score drops below 70%, Testim automatically attempts to improve it, replacing the degraded locator and logging a 'Testim auto improve' revision on success — it doesn't immediately fail the test, skip the element, or delete the locator.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What happens when the attributes of an element are changed during a test run?

options.text: The test will automatically fail.
The test may pass, but the confidence score may decrease.
The test will become more stable.
The test will skip the changed element..

practiceQuiz.hint: Smart Locators can usually still find the element using other attributes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Smart Locators weight many attributes per element, so a test can still pass when some attributes change — using the remaining unchanged attributes — but the confidence score for that locator may decrease. It doesn't automatically fail, become more stable, or skip the element outright.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What must be done first before you can capture video in Testim for a bug scenario?

options.text: Ensure the video capture feature is enabled in the Testim settings.
Add a validation step to the test case.
Install the Testim browser extension for Chrome.
Create a bug report template in the Testim dashboard.

practiceQuiz.hint: The capture/video functionality lives inside the extension, not the web editor.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Capture Video & Bug Scenario is a feature of the Testim Chrome Extension, so installing that extension is the required first step — it isn't a setting toggle, a validation step, or a bug report template, which are separate concerns that come after the extension is in place.

quickRecap.value: Draft, Active, Evaluating, Quarantine — not 'Failed' or 'Archived'.
Single-location vs. multi-tag, searchable via label:<name>.
Advanced filters surface hidden steps (and filter by Groups/Actions/Validations/Wait for).
Auto-created on every save — no manual trigger.
Model setup/teardown; integrate with CI by picking a specific tool and running through its pipeline.
Group into collections + control run order (guaranteed only without --parallel).
Score < 70% → auto-attempted improvement, logged as a revision.
Changed attributes → test may still pass, but confidence can drop.
Capture Video & Bug Scenario requires the Testim Chrome Extension installed first.
